item.title: CVE-2026-128981 - NVD - CVSS: não informado
item.description:
Wednesday 18 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS: não informado | ** UNSUPPORTED WHEN ASSIGNED **
Improper Authentication in Apache SeaTunnel Web 1.0.2 allows a user whose account has been disabled to authenticate with valid credentials and obtain a new login token. The login query does not check the account status, so disabling an account does not prevent new logins or access to protected APIs using the newly issued token. This issue requires valid credentials for the disabled account; it is not a credential-free authentication bypass.
Apache SeaTunnel Web is no longer maintained. The affected 1.0.2 release does not contain the account-status check added to the main branch in pull request #264. There is no maintained fixed release. Users should discontinue use of this unsupported component.
NOTE: This vulnerability only affects products that are no longer supported by the maintainer.

item.title: CVE-2026-99312 - NVD - CVSS: não informado
item.description:
Wednesday 18 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS: não informado | In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
KVM: x86: Unconditionally reset MMU context when emulating INIT
Force an MMU reset when emulating an INIT even if paging was already disabled, as the MMU page role includes guest_mode (L2), i.e. an INIT while L2 is running with CR0.PG=0 will result in KVM running L1 with a stale MMU context.
Alternatively, the reset could be scoped strictly to paging being enabled or L2 being active, but SMM is also encoded in the page role. Even though it _should_ be impossible for the vCPU to be INIT'd while SMM is active, there's zero value in not handling SMM. At that point, the only scenario where KVM _doesn't_ need to reset the MMU context is on an INIT with the vCPU running in Real Mode or Unpaged Protect Mode, and while INIT in those modes is somewhat common, it's far from a hot path and re-initializing the MMU is not expensive, especially when the role isn't changing (KVM elides most of the re-configuration in that case).
Note, like the Fixes commit, this bug only affects nested SVM as INIT is an unconditional intercept on VMX, i.e. it's impossible to emulate INIT while L2 is active.
Temporarily keep the guest TLB flush when CR0.PG is being cleared even though it is fully redundant with the flush that is emitted on all INIT events (KVM itself only does RESET when a vCPU is being created, i.e. when CR0.PG must be '0').

item.title: CVE-2026-99313 - NVD - CVSS: não informado
item.description:
Wednesday 18 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS: não informado | In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
HID: logitech-hidpp: fix race condition when accessing stale stack pointer
The driver uses hidpp->send_receive_buf to point to a stack-allocated buffer in the synchronous command path (__do_hidpp_send_message_sync). However, this pointer is not cleared when the function returns.
If an event is processed (e.g. by a different thread) while the send_mutex is held by a new command, but before that command has updated send_receive_buf, the handler (hidpp_raw_hidpp_event) will observe that the mutex is locked and dereference the stale pointer.
This results in an out-of-bounds access on a different thread's kernel stack (or a NULL pointer dereference on the very first command).
Fix this by: 1. Clearing hidpp->send_receive_buf to NULL before releasing the mutex in the synchronous command path. 2. Moving the assignment of the local 'question' and 'answer' pointers inside the mutex_is_locked() block in the handler, and adding a NULL check before dereferencing.

item.title: CVE-2026-99314 - NVD - CVSS: não informado
item.description:
Wednesday 18 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS: não informado | In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
ALSA: us122l: Add missing NULL check in usb_stream_hwdep_mmap()
usb_stream_hwdep_mmap() reads us122l->sk.s and dereferences it without checking for NULL. The stream object is released by usb_stream_free(), which is reached through us122l_stop() both when the device is disconnected and when us122l_start() fails, and it leaves us122l->sk.s set to NULL. The hwdep file stays usable after that, so a later mmap()
KASAN: null-ptr-deref in range [0x0000000000000010-0x0000000000000017] RIP: 0010:usb_stream_hwdep_mmap+0x107/0x890 sound/usb/usx2y/us122l.c:182
crashes while reading s->read_size, which sits at offset 0x10.
That NULL is an expected state for this field: usb_stream_hwdep_vm_fault(), usb_stream_hwdep_poll(), usb_stream_hwdep_ioctl(), usb_stream_stop() and usb_stream_free() all test it before use. Only the mmap callback misses the check, so let it return -ENODEV, matching what the other hwdep mapping in usx2yhwdeppcm.c does when its shared buffer has not been allocated.

item.title: CVE-2026-99315 - NVD - CVSS: não informado
item.description:
Wednesday 18 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS: não informado | In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
ALSA: us122l: Fix NULL dereference at hwdep open and release
usb_stream_hwdep_open() and usb_stream_hwdep_release() pass the result of usb_ifnum_to_if() straight to usb_autopm_get_interface() and usb_autopm_put_interface(), without checking it for NULL.
usb_ifnum_to_if() returns NULL once the device is gone, since usb_disable_device() clears udev->actconfig on disconnect. The hwdep file can outlive the disconnect: the card is released with snd_card_free_when_closed(), so a process that keeps the character device open reaches the driver's release callback after the USB configuration has been dropped, and interface_to_usbdev() then dereferences the NULL interface at offsetof(struct device, parent). The open callback has the same problem when it races with the disconnect.
Check both lookups and fail the open with -ENODEV; in release, skip the runtime PM put when the interface is already gone and still run the rest of the per-file cleanup. Move the us122l->first bookkeeping after the checks so that a failed open no longer leaves a stale file pointer behind.

item.title: CVE-2026-99316 - NVD - CVSS: não informado
item.description:
Wednesday 18 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS: não informado | In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
ALSA: usx2y: Initialize idle URBs before submitting streams
usb_stream_start() submits the first two capture and playback URBs and only afterwards assigns sk->idle_inurb, sk->idle_outurb, sk->completed_inurb and sk->completed_outurb to the remaining two URBs of each direction.
A transfer can complete as soon as usb_submit_urb() has been called, so the completion handler i_capture_start() or i_playback_start() may run before those pointers are set. While the stream is still being synchronized (state below usb_stream_sync1), stream_start() then calls playback_prep_freqn(sk, sk->idle_outurb) with sk->idle_outurb still NULL, and the packet descriptors are written through that NULL pointer:
Oops: general protection fault, probably for non-canonical address 0xdffffc0000000018: 0000 [#1] SMP KASAN KASAN: null-ptr-deref in range [0x00000000000000c0-0x00000000000000c7] RIP: 0010:playback_prep_freqn+0x11c/0x4a0 sound/usb/usx2y/usb_stream.c:33 Call Trace: <IRQ> stream_start+0x5dc/0x8d0 sound/usb/usx2y/usb_stream.c:596 i_capture_start+0x3da/0x710 sound/usb/usx2y/usb_stream.c:654 __usb_hcd_giveback_urb+0x238/0x550 drivers/usb/core/hcd.c:1657 usb_giveback_urb_bh+0x20b/0x530 drivers/usb/core/hcd.c:1691 tasklet_hi_action+0xa/0x20 kernel/softirq.c:994 handle_softirqs+0x16f/0x440 kernel/softirq.c:645 </IRQ>
The four URBs referenced by these pointers are allocated long before and do not depend on any transfer state, so assign them before the submit loop. Keeping the assignment inside the retry path also restores a well-defined URB rotation when the start frame mismatch handling kills and resubmits the streams.

item.title: CVE-2026-99317 - NVD - CVSS: não informado
item.description:
Wednesday 18 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS: não informado | In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
ALSA: hwdep: Serialize DSP load requests
The check of the loaded DSP indices and the call of the driver's dsp_load callback in snd_hwdep_dsp_load() are not serialized. A hwdep file descriptor can be shared among threads, or inherited across fork, so two SNDRV_HWDEP_IOCTL_DSP_LOAD requests for the same index can both observe the index as unloaded and enter the driver's callback concurrently, even though the device itself is opened exclusively.
This breaks the assumption behind hw->dsp_loaded that a firmware index is loaded only once. For example, snd-usb-usx2y hits WARN_ON(usx2y->as04.buffer) in usx2y_async_seq04_init() and may allocate the US-428 sequence URBs twice.
Serialize the check, the callback invocation and the bookkeeping with a per-hwdep mutex, so that the second request returns -EBUSY.

item.title: CVE-2026-99318 - NVD - CVSS: não informado
item.description:
Wednesday 18 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS: não informado | In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
ALSA: bcd2000: Fix use-after-free of MIDI URBs on file close
bcd2000_disconnect() calls snd_card_disconnect(), which only prevents new opens, and then frees the MIDI URBs. A rawmidi file that was already open can still be closed afterwards, and its close callback, bcd2000_midi_output_close(), calls usb_kill_urb() on midi_out_urb.
The URB pointers are cleared on disconnect and their accesses are serialized with midi_lock, but bcd2000_midi_output_close() reads midi_out_urb without that lock. The check can therefore pass just before the pointer is cleared, and usb_kill_urb() then runs on the URB that has already been freed:
BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in usb_kill_urb+0x74/0x80 Read of size 8 at addr ffff8880078e7d40 usb_kill_urb bcd2000_midi_output_close close_substream rawmidi_release_priv snd_rawmidi_release
Allocated by: usb_alloc_urb <- bcd2000_init_midi <- bcd2000_probe Freed by: usb_free_urb <- bcd2000_midi_free <- bcd2000_disconnect
Take the lock in bcd2000_midi_output_close() and reference the URB with usb_get_urb() before releasing it. The URB then stays valid until usb_put_urb() after usb_kill_urb() has returned, even if a disconnect frees it in the meantime. usb_kill_urb() itself cannot run under midi_lock, as the completion handler takes the same lock.

item.title: CVE-2026-99319 - NVD - CVSS: não informado
item.description:
Wednesday 18 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS: não informado | In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
ALSA: usx2y: Refuse a retried DSP load after a failure
snd_usx2y_hwdep_dsp_load() sets up the asynchronous sequence URBs and the interrupt URB when the FPGA firmware image with index 1 is loaded, and then creates the ALSA devices. If usx2y_in04_init() or usx2y_create_alsa_devices() fails, the URBs that were already set up are left in place.
The core keeps the index unloaded when the callback fails, so user space may issue the same request again. The second attempt then enters usx2y_async_seq04_init() or usx2y_in04_init() with the URBs still allocated and trips WARN_ON(usx2y->as04.buffer) or WARN_ON(usx2y->in04_urb).
The URBs cannot be released at this point: the card may already have registered PCM devices that user space can still open, and the disconnect handler accesses the URBs without holding the DSP lock. Mark the chip as hung instead, so that a retried request is refused with -ENODEV and the assertions keep their meaning. The URBs are released by snd_usx2y_card_private_free() when the card is freed.
A failing usx2y_async_seq04_init() still releases its own URBs, so that path remains retryable.

item.title: CVE-2026-110513 - NVD - CVSS: não informado
item.description:
Wednesday 18 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS: não informado | Insufficient Session Expiration vulnerability in the Apache Iggy server HTTP transport. A self-issued JSON Web Token (JWT) identified the user only by numeric user ID, and a new user takes the lowest free ID. After an administrator deleted a user, that user's unexpired token, or a token refreshed from it while the ID was free, authenticated as the next account created with that ID and had that account's permissions. Only deployments with HTTP enabled are affected.
This issue affects Apache Iggy: through 0.9.0.
Users are recommended to upgrade to version 0.10.0, which fixes the issue.

item.title: CVE-2026-112213 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 6.9
item.description: Wednesday 18 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 6.9 | Out-of-bounds read vulnerability in the pixReadMemJp2kCore() function in Leptonica, located in jp2kio.c. The function retrieves the output dimensions only for component 0 and uses a common index to iterate through the buffers of all components. If the remaining components have smaller dimensions, the traversal exceeds the bounds of their sample buffers, which are allocated by OpenJPEG. When processing a specially crafted JPEG 2000 image, data read from adjacent dynamic memory may be incorporated into the pixels of the decoded image and result in information disclosure to anyone who can access the output.

item.title: CVE-2026-120557 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 6.4
item.description: Wednesday 18 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 6.4 | The WP Delicious – Recipe Plugin for Food Bloggers (formerly Delicious Recipes) plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'details[].icon' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.10.11 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The payload bypasses wp_kses_post on save because Gutenberg serializes block attribute JSON with JSON_HEX_QUOT, encoding double-quotes as \u0022 so no raw quote or angle bracket appears in post_content; parse_blocks() restores the literal quote at render time, producing the HTML attribute breakout.

item.title: CVE-2026-120566 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 6.4
item.description: Wednesday 18 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 6.4 | The WP Delicious – Recipe Plugin for Food Bloggers (formerly Delicious Recipes) plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'recipeTitle' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.10.10 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. WordPress core's block-attribute kses pass strips HTML tags but preserves bare double-quote characters, allowing a payload such as x" onerror="alert(1) to survive both the save pipeline and the render-time strip_tags() call, breaking out of the alt attribute of the rendered img element.

item.title: CVE-2026-123343 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 6.5
item.description: Wednesday 18 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 6.5 | The BlockArt Blocks – Gutenberg Blocks, Page Builder Blocks ,WordPress Block Plugin, Sections & Template Library plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to authorization bypass in all versions up to, and including, 2.4.3. This is due to the plugin not properly verifying that a user is authorized to perform an action. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to view the title, excerpt, and full content of other users' draft, pending, and private posts, exposing that content to unauthenticated visitors on the published permalink. This is exploitable by an Author-level user because WordPress's wp_filter_post_kses preserves block-comment JSON in HTML comments, allowing the malicious queryArgs and query[post_status] attributes to survive post saving and execute on every unauthenticated request to the published URL. Exploitation by attackers with contributor-level access and above requires that attacker only needs to see the data themselves (not expose it to unauthenticated visitors) — satisfied by viewing their own preview URL. On a default installation, where that is not configured, the vulnerability requires attackers with author-level access and above.

item.title: CVE-2026-125012 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 6.4
item.description: Wednesday 18 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 6.4 | The Flying Images: Optimize and Lazy Load Images for Faster Page Speed plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'post_content' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.4.16 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Although wp_kses_post sanitizes post content on save, the payload is kses-legal at save time; the plugin's output-buffer rewrite transforms it into an executable form at render time by overwriting the valueless data-src attribute with the unescaped src value, meaning save-time sanitization provides no effective mitigation.

item.title: CVE-2026-129509 - NVD - CVSS: não informado
item.description: Wednesday 18 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS: não informado | In the Apache Airflow Microsoft Azure provider 10.2.0 through 15.3.0, `S3ToAzureBlobStorageOperator` turned off TLS certificate verification for its connection to Amazon S3 by default (`s3_verify=False`), whatever the AWS connection's own verification settings were. An attacker positioned on the network between an Airflow worker and S3 could intercept that traffic, read the signed requests and alter the listed object keys and the copied file contents. item.title: CVE-2026-19707 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 9.5
item.description:
Wednesday 18 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 9.5 | A bug in the Airlock Gateway (8.5.2 and earlier, and 8.6.0) allows attacker-controlled HTML in a backend response to exploit the Smart Form Protection feature, possibly leading to a Denial of Service (DoS) or Remote Code Execution (RCE) attack against the Airlock Gateway. The issue has been fixed in Airlock Gateway version 8.5.3 and 8.6.1.
For an attack to be executable, the Airlock Gateway needs to have 'Smart Form Protection' (or the corresponding expert settings) enabled on a mapping whose backend returns a response containing certain multi-byte HTML character references. The buffer overflow then happens during the parsing of that HTML response. Such a response can come either from a malicious or compromised backend, or from an otherwise trusted backend that returns attacker-supplied HTML, e.g. an application that stores and serves plain user-provided HTML files.
Successfully exploiting the vulnerability can enable an attacker to perform a DoS attack or, in the worst case, an RCE attack against the Airlock Gateway in front of the affected backend. Compromising the functionality of the Airlock Gateway could in this way also affect the availability and protection of other well-intentioned backends deployed behind the same Gateway.

item.title: CVE-2026-110486 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 9.8
item.description: Wednesday 18 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 9.8 | In Eclipse Mosquitto versions 2.1 through 2.1.2, a listener configured with `protocol websockets` mishandles empty WebSocket data frames. `net__read_ws()` in `lib/net_ws.c` returns the number of framing bytes consumed (the 4 masking-key bytes) for a data frame with a zero-length payload, without writing any bytes to the caller’s buffer. The MQTT packet reader in `packet__read_single()` (`lib/packet_mosq.c`) trusts that return value as a payload byte count. A remote client can therefore advance the read position over an uninitialised heap allocation, causing the broker to process and forward uninitialised heap memory (information disclosure, including heap and libc pointers), and can underflow the unsigned `to_process` counter so that subsequent attacker-controlled frame data is written past the end of the allocation (heap out-of-bounds write). The out-of-bounds write is reachable from the CONNECT packet before any authentication check, so an unauthenticated client can corrupt the heap and crash the broker even when `allow_anonymous false` is set. Combining the disclosure and the write allows remote code execution as the broker’s user by any client able to establish a session.

item.title: CVE-2026-132049 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 4.3
item.description: Wednesday 18 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 4.3 | A flaw was found in lldpd. The service fails to verify that Link Layer Discovery Protocol - Media Endpoint Discovery (LLDP-MED) location records received from network neighbors match their declared lengths. An adjacent attacker on the local network can exploit this flaw by sending crafted packets, causing client applications using the liblldpctl library to read past buffer boundaries when parsing location data. This issue can lead to an information disclosure of adjacent process memory.

item.title: CVE-2026-132069 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 6.3
item.description:
Wednesday 18 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 6.3 | MISP (Malware Information Sharing Platform) contains an authorization bypass in the SharingGroup model's captureSGExisting method. The authorization check used a logical AND condition that effectively exempted users with the sync permission (perm_sync) from the membership verification. Specifically, the original condition 'if (!checkIfAuthorised(...) && !perm_sync) return false' meant that any user holding the sync role would pass the check regardless of whether they were actually a member of the target sharing group.
A sync user who knows or can discover the UUID of a non-local sharing group could exploit this flaw through the /sharing_groups/add endpoint or by embedding a SharingGroup object in pushed sync data. The attacker could rewrite the sharing group record to add their own organisation as a member or insert an all_orgs server entry for their MISP instance, thereby gaining read access to all events contained in that group. This exposes threat intelligence data that was intended to be restricted to the group's legitimate members.
The vulnerability requires an authenticated account with the sync role and knowledge of a valid sharing group UUID. No user interaction is required. The impact is unauthorized disclosure of shared threat intelligence events and limited integrity modification of the sharing group record.
